milestones.headline: Smoke on the horizon
milestones.body: A column of smoke rises from the valley for the first time by somebody's deliberate choice. Nobody is around to write it down, but the atmosphere is keeping score.

milestones.headline: The first field is cleared
milestones.body: A stretch of forest is burned back and planted. It feeds more people than the forest did — and it is the first time anyone has decided what a landscape is for.

milestones.headline: Steam and iron remake the world
milestones.body: Mills that never sleep, cities black with soot, and coal hauled out of the ground faster than anyone can count it. Progress, they are calling it.

milestones.headline: Coal smog kills thousands in a week
milestones.body: A temperature inversion has trapped a city's chimney smoke at street level. Physicians report the death toll is highest among the men who dig the coal.

milestones.headline: River declared "biologically dead" below the mills
milestones.body: Steelworks upstream have discharged for a decade into water that fishermen worked for a thousand years. An inquiry has been promised, then postponed.

milestones.headline: Factories switch to continuous production
milestones.body: The line no longer stops at night. Output has doubled twice in a year, and the coal to run it is being burned as fast as it can be shovelled.

milestones.headline: City lights up for the first time
milestones.body: A coal-fired station on the edge of town has electrified a whole district. Crowds gathered to watch. Nobody looked at the chimney.

milestones.headline: Oil strike opens a new age of fuel
milestones.body: Crude is coming out of the ground faster than it can be barrelled. Analysts predict the supply is, for practical purposes, infinite.

milestones.headline: A car in every driveway
milestones.body: Private motoring has gone from a curiosity to an expectation in a generation. Cities are being rebuilt around it, and the exhaust is being described as the smell of prosperity.

milestones.headline: A hole is found in the ozone layer
milestones.body: Refrigerant gases invented to be harmless turn out to destroy stratospheric ozone on contact. Industry has called the finding "premature".

milestones.headline: World's first 30-million-person city
milestones.body: Concrete, steel and air conditioning have made a metropolis possible where the climate never was. Both the concrete and the cooling are enormously carbon-intensive; neither is mentioned at the ribbon-cutting.

milestones.headline: Fracking unlocks "a century of cheap gas"
milestones.body: Shale wells are producing at rates nobody forecast. Residents downwind report they can set their tap water alight; the industry disputes the connection.

milestones.headline: Livestock population passes human population
milestones.body: Industrial husbandry now runs more cattle than there are people to eat them. Methane from their digestion has become a measurable share of global emissions.

milestones.headline: Global shipping now moves more than nations produce
milestones.body: Standardised steel boxes have made distance almost free. Freighters burn the heaviest, dirtiest fraction of the barrel to do it.

milestones.headline: The world connects itself
milestones.body: Everyone alive can now be told anything, instantly. Among the first things widely circulated is the evidence for what the burning is doing.

milestones.headline: Data centres overtake aviation for electricity use
milestones.body: The buildings that hold the world's information draw more power than the world's aeroplanes. Almost all of it is generated by burning something.

milestones.headline: Mass air travel becomes routine
milestones.body: Millions are now airborne at any moment, each of them emitting at an altitude where it does the most harm.

milestones.headline: CO₂ higher than at any point in 800,000 years
milestones.body: Ice cores hold a continuous record of the atmosphere going back eight hundred millennia. This week's reading is off the top of it.

milestones.headline: CO₂ passes 350 ppm — "the safe ceiling"
milestones.body: Climatologists have long called 350 parts per million the upper limit for a stable climate. The needle went through it this morning and kept going.

milestones.headline: World blows past the 1.5 °C limit
milestones.body: The threshold at the heart of every climate treaty ever signed has been crossed. Delegates are expected to negotiate a new, higher threshold.

milestones.headline: Carbon dioxide breaks 400 ppm
milestones.body: The last time the atmosphere held this much CO₂, there were forests near the South Pole. Officials have described the reading as "a milestone" and declined to say of what.

milestones.headline: The Amazon is on fire
milestones.body: Record heat and record drought have turned the world's largest rainforest into kindling. Smoke plumes are visible from orbit; the forest that spent ten thousand years absorbing carbon is now releasing it.

milestones.headline: Great Barrier Reef declared functionally dead
milestones.body: Marine biologists confirm that ocean heat and acidification have bleached the last resilient reef sections. "We are no longer studying an ecosystem," one researcher said. "We are studying a ruin."

milestones.headline: Arctic recorded ice-free in summer
milestones.body: For the first time in human history, satellites found open water at the North Pole in September. Shipping companies have called the news "an opportunity".

milestones.headline: Simultaneous harvest failure across three continents
milestones.body: Heat and drought have hit the world's breadbaskets in the same season. Grain prices have tripled and export bans are spreading faster than aid.

milestones.headline: Deadly wet-bulb conditions strike South Asia
milestones.body: Humid heat has passed the limit at which a human body can cool itself. Authorities have advised 400 million people to remain indoors, where there is no power for cooling.

milestones.headline: Miami, Jakarta and Alexandria begin permanent evacuation
milestones.body: Sea walls have been overtopped for the third year running. Three coastal megacities are being abandoned rather than defended — the first of many, planners concede.

milestones.headline: Siberian permafrost is venting methane
milestones.body: Ground frozen for forty thousand years is collapsing into craters and releasing the carbon inside it. The thaw now adds more greenhouse gas each year than it can be stopped from adding.

milestones.headline: Global insect populations collapse
milestones.body: Pollinator numbers have fallen below the level agriculture depends on. Orchards in four countries are being pollinated by hand.

milestones.headline: Amazon rainforest passes point of no return
milestones.body: Ecologists confirm the dieback is self-sustaining: what is left of the forest is now drying itself out. The basin is becoming savanna, and every dying tree adds to the problem.

milestones.headline: CO₂ passes 500 ppm; monitoring stations begin closing
milestones.body: Two long-running observatories have gone offline this month, one to fire and one to funding. The remaining stations report the curve is steepening.

milestones.headline: Atlantic overturning circulation has stalled
milestones.body: The current that keeps northern Europe temperate has slowed to a stop. Meteorologists warn of winters no living person has experienced, in a world that is otherwise cooking.

milestones.headline: One billion people are now displaced
milestones.body: The UN refugee agency has stopped publishing a running total, saying the figure "changes faster than it can be verified".

milestones.headline: CO₂ passes 1,000 ppm — beyond every published projection
milestones.body: The concentration has left the range any climate model was built to handle. Researchers are extrapolating, with the caveat that extrapolation is all anyone has left.

milestones.headline: Oceans declared largely lifeless
milestones.body: Acidification has dissolved the base of the marine food web. Fisheries worldwide have closed; the sea, for the first time, is quiet.

milestones.headline: Five metres of sea level rise; coastlines redrawn
milestones.body: Cartographers have begun issuing world maps annually rather than by edition. Most of the world's ports, and the industry that fed them, are underwater.

milestones.headline: Heat forces cascading failure of the global grid
milestones.body: Transmission lines sag, transformers fail, and the cooling systems fail with them. Industry continues regardless, on generators.

milestones.headline: Final scheduled news broadcast airs
milestones.body: With habitability in single digits, the last continuously operating newsroom has gone dark. Its closing line: "Whatever it was you were doing, it worked."

milestones.headline: Astronomers begin comparing Earth to Venus
milestones.body: At current forcing, the paper notes, the distinction is "increasingly a matter of degree". Peer review has been waived for lack of reviewers.
